provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: God made me special
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state one special thing about themselves.
The pupils should be able to identify something they can do well.
Introduction:
We are all special in our own way.
God made each of us different.
Content:
Every child is special and unique.
God made you with special abilities.
You can do things others cannot do.
For example, you can sing or draw well.
You are special because you are you.
Class activity:
Each pupil will stand up and say one thing they can do well.
The class will clap for each pupil.
Evaluation questions:
What makes you special?
What can you do well?
How did God make you special?
Summary:
God made you special and unique.

topics.title: Saying thank you
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say thank you when given something.
The pupils should be able to identify when to say thank you.
Introduction:
We have received gifts from people before.
We need to show gratitude.
Content:
When someone gives you something, say thank you.
Say thank you with a big smile.
For example, when mummy gives you food.
Or when a friend shares a toy with you.
Thank you is a magic word.
Class activity:
The teacher will give pupils small objects.
Each pupil will practice saying thank you with a smile.
Evaluation questions:
What do you say when someone gives you something?
When should you say thank you?
Show me how to say thank you with a smile.
Summary:
Always say thank you when you receive something.

topics.title: Saying please
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use please when asking for something.
The pupils should be able to role - play asking politely.
Introduction:
Sometimes we need help from others.
We must ask kindly.
Content:
When you want something, say please.
For example, please may I have water?
Please is a polite word to use.
It shows good manners.
Always use please when asking.
Class activity:
Pupils will role - play asking for toys politely.
Each pupil will practice saying please.
Evaluation questions:
What do you say when you want something?
Show how to ask for water politely.
Why should we use please?
Summary:
Always say please when asking for something.

topics.title: Truthful words
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to tell the truth always.
The pupils should be able to explain why truth is important.
Introduction:
Sometimes we tell stories that are not true.
We must learn to tell the truth.
Content:
Always say what really happened.
The truth is the best thing to say.
For example, if you break a cup, say it.
Telling the truth shows you are good.
Lying is not a good habit.
Class activity:
The teacher will tell a short story about truth.
Pupils will practice saying the truth in situations.
Evaluation questions:
What should you always say?
Why is truth important?
What happens when you tell lies?
Summary:
Always tell the truth no matter what.

topics.title: Gentle hands
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to touch friends gently.
The pupils should be able to identify how to use hands well.
Introduction:
Our hands are very useful.
We must use them well.
Content:
Touch your friends gently.
Hands are for helping not hurting.
For example, when playing with friends.
Use hands to help carry books.
Do not hit or push with your hands.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice touching gently.
Each pupil will show how to help with hands.
Evaluation questions:
How should we touch our friends?
What are hands used for?
Show how to use hands to help.
Summary:
Always use your hands to help gently.

topics.title: Obedience
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to listen to adults.
The pupils should be able to obey the first time.
Introduction:
Adults tell us what to do for our good.
We must listen and obey.
Content:
Listen to mummy, daddy and teacher.
Do what they say the first time.
For example, when teacher says sit down.
Obeying keeps you safe and happy.
Do not argue or delay.
Class activity:
The teacher will give simple instructions.
Pupils will practice obeying immediately.
Evaluation questions:
Who should you listen to?
What should you do when given instructions?
Why is obedience important?
Summary:
Always obey adults the first time.

topics.title: Cleanliness
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to keep their body clean.
The pupils should be able to identify clean habits.
Introduction:
We want to be healthy and happy.
Cleanliness helps us stay healthy.
Content:
Keep your body and class clean.
For example, wash your hands before eating.
Put rubbish in the bin.
Clean habits make you feel good.
Dirty places can make you sick.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice washing hands properly.
Each pupil will show how to keep the class clean.
Evaluation questions:
How do we keep our body clean?
Why is cleanliness important?
Show how to wash hands.
Summary:
Always keep yourself and your environment clean.

topics.title: Loving my friends
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to be kind to everyone.
The pupils should be able to invite a new friend to play.
Introduction:
Friends make us happy.
We must love and care for them.
Content:
Be kind to everyone.
For example, share your toys with friends.\ Invite a new friend to play.
Loving friends means being nice to them.
Do not leave anyone out when playing.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice inviting others to play.
Each pupil will say something kind to a friend.
Evaluation questions:
How should we treat our friends?
What does loving friends mean?
Show how to invite someone to play.
Summary:
Always be kind and loving to your friends.

topics.title: Forgiving
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to say I forgive you.
The pupils should be able to play with friends after forgiving.
Introduction:
Sometimes friends hurt us.
We need to learn to forgive.
Content:
When someone says sorry, say I forgive you.
For example, if a friend takes your toy.
Forgiving helps you make up.
Play again together after forgiving.
Class activity:
Pupils will practice saying I forgive you.
Each pupil will role - play forgiving a friend.
Evaluation questions:
What do you say when someone says sorry?
Why is forgiving important?
Show how to forgive a friend.
Summary:
Always forgive others and be friends again.

topics.title: Revision and story day
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall moral lessons.
The pupils should be able to participate in moral songs.
Introduction:
We have learned many good things.
Today we will revise and have fun.
Content:
Story of the good boy or girl.
Sing our moral songs.
Remember to say please and thank you.
Always tell the truth and be kind.
Keep your hands gentle and clean.
Class activity:
The teacher will tell a story about good behavior.
Pupils will sing moral songs together.
Evaluation questions:
What did we learn about saying thank you?
Why is it important to be truthful?
Show how to be kind to friends.
Summary:
Let us always remember our good lessons.
